question.problem: In what direction does the function $f(x,y)=2(xy+1)^{3/2}$ increase most rapidly at the point $(3,1)?$
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(3,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2(xy+1)^{3/2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2(xy+1)^{3/2})\,j \\  & =3y\sqrt{xy+1}\,i+3x\sqrt{xy+1}\,j \\ ∇f(3,1) & =3(1)\sqrt{(3)(1)+1}\,i+3(3)\sqrt{(3)(1)+1}\,j \\  & =6\,i+18\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of $6\,i+18\,j.$
